precepts.text: Haman, a Macedonian, a stranger from the Persian blood: Philip was the Macedonian, so Edomites and Macedonians are the same people, and Haman was an Edomite.
precepts.point: Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite: Agag was the Amalekite king of 1 Samuel 15, so Haman descended from the Edomites Saul failed to finish, and when he learned Mordecai was of Saul's line he sought to kill them all. From the womb to the tomb, this is war.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Esther 3:1 calls Haman the Agagite. Chapter 16 tells you what he was: “For Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood”. Haman was a Macedonian.

Now read 1 Maccabees 1:1: “Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian”. Alexander the Great's father was Philip the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettiim and whose son smote Darius king of the Persians and Medes and reigned in his stead, the first over Greece. That is when the Greeks began to conquer the dark nations.

So Haman was called a Macedonian, and Philip was called the Macedonian: Edomites and Macedonians are the same people. Haman was not a Persian; he was “a stranger from the Persian blood”. He was an Edomite, the Agagite, a descendant of Amalek, the enemy of Jacob from generation to generation.

precepts.text: Almighty God turned to joy the day wherein the chosen people should have perished, and they were told to keep it among their solemn feasts as a high day. Purim is a feast for God allowing us to kill our enemies, so what do you mean we are not to rejoice over the fall of the nations trying to destroy us?
precepts.point: Rome, you just slaughtered a thousand Israelites, let me pray for you, is the stupidest thought there is, and it is the idea the black Christian holds and preaches.

precepts.text: This Apocrypha verse shows Aman was not of Persian blood but a Macedonian, a stranger received among them.
precepts.point: The teaching traces who Aman was. He is the same Aman promoted in the canonical book, an Agagite, and the Agagites descend from Agag king of the Amalekites, and Amalek descends from Esau. This is the lineage that has warred against Israel throughout history and has always been unsuccessful, for the Most High delivered his people.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
Aman was in great honour with the king, but he was not one of the king's own people. The king's second letter says so: “Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood, and far distant from our goodness, and as a stranger received of us”. He was a Macedonian, a stranger from the Persian blood, received among the Persians and lifted up by them.

So the man who sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs was a stranger in the kingdom, an Agagite of the stock of Agag the Amalekite, of Esau, not a Persian. The honour he held was given him by a people he did not belong to, and he turned it against Israel.

precepts.text: The Most High chose Israel to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.
precepts.point: Therefore the first letters sent by Haman are not to be executed, for Haman himself is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family, the Most High rendering vengeance according to his deserts. The copy of this second letter is to be published everywhere so the Jews may live after their own laws and, on the thirteenth day of Adar, be avenged on those who set upon them.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The king's second letter finds the Jews “are no evildoers, but live by most just laws: And that they be children of the most high and most mighty, living God, who hath ordered the kingdom both unto us and to our progenitors in the most excellent manner.” A heathen king writes to every province that Israel are the children of the living God. That is the plain testimony of scripture concerning who Israel is.

The Most High said it first: “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Israel is his chosen, peculiar people, above all the nations. The first letter called them a malicious people whose laws were contrary to all nations; the second says the opposite, that their laws are most just and their God is the most high and most mighty. The king's letter caught up with what the Lord had already declared.

precepts.text: The king gave Esther the house of Haman and Mardocheus his ring, and let them write a decree in the king's name to reverse Haman's letters.
precepts.point: Therefore the first letters sent by Haman are not to be executed, for Haman himself is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family, the Most High rendering vengeance according to his deserts. The copy of this second letter is to be published everywhere so the Jews may live after their own laws and, on the thirteenth day of Adar, be avenged on those who set upon them.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The second letter tells the provinces not to execute “the letters sent unto you by Aman the son of Amadatha”, because “he that was the worker of these things, is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family: God, who ruleth all things, speedily rendering vengeance to him according to his deserts.”

The canonical book shows the king giving the order. “Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews. Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.” Haman's letters had been sealed with the king's ring and could not be reversed; so the king gave Esther the house of Haman and Mardocheus the ring, and let them write a decree in his name that answered the first.

That decree is this letter: published in all places, “that the Jews may freely live after their own laws”, and that on the thirteenth day of Adar “they may be avenged on them, who in the time of their affliction shall set upon them.” Vengeance came to Haman according to his deserts, and the reversal to Israel.

precepts.text: Enquire of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers.
precepts.point: This is the same lesson for our people today. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Search out the former age and the fathers, for this is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
“For Almighty God hath turned to joy unto them the day, wherein the chosen people should have perished.” That is why this is written down and kept: it is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Search out the former age and the fathers. What the Most High did for Israel in Persia, turning the day of death into a day of joy, is what he does. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Esther's day is the former age we enquire of to know that.

precepts.point: This is the same lesson for our people today. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The king commands the Jews to keep this day “among your solemn feasts” as “an high day with all feasting”. The canonical book records that feasting: “in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day.”

The same provinces where the first decree had brought mourning now had joy and gladness. Almighty God turned the day to joy, and wherever the decree came the Jews kept it as a feast and a good day. “And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.” The fear that had been on Israel fell on the people of the land instead: the “safety to us” of the letter, and the “memorial of destruction” to those that conspired.

precepts.text: The days were kept as the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month turned from sorrow to joy, with feasting and gifts to the poor.
precepts.point: This is the same lesson for our people today. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Search out the former age and the fathers, for this is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The day the chosen people should have perished became a feast. The canonical book names what the feast remembers: “the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.”

Sorrow to joy, mourning into a good day: that is Almighty God turning the day to joy, kept with feasting, portions sent one to another and gifts to the poor. And it is the same lesson for our people today. We are in days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord; the month that turned for them will turn for us.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

He thought to translate the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.
